title: Solid oral forms, the 60-day supply ceiling and the as-needed exclusion for multi-drug-single-dose packaging
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.08(3), a pharmacy or pharmacist may utilize multi-drug-single-dose packaging for solid oral dosage forms provided the following requirements are met: under (a), a licensee may not dispense more than a 60-day supply of medication in a multi-drug-single-dose package; under (b), a licensee may not dispense Schedules II or III controlled substances in a multi-drug-single-dose package; and under (c), a licensee may not dispense medications to be taken on an as needed basis in a multi-drug-single-dose package.
exam_relevance: Tests the three limits that sit on multi-drug-single-dose packaging in addition to the general compliance packaging conditions: the 60-day supply ceiling, the Schedule II and III exclusion, and the exclusion of medications taken as needed, all within solid oral dosage forms.

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum supply in a multi-drug-single-dose package

common_confusions: Placing an as-needed medication in the same multi-drug-single-dose package as scheduled doses.
Treating the 60-day ceiling as a limit on beyond-use dating only; it is also a limit on the supply dispensed.
